mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about reference frames is incorrect?

options.A: A reference frame can be either stationary or moving with constant velocity relative to an observer.
options.B: In a non‑inertial reference frame, Newton’s first law does not hold without introducing fictitious forces.
options.C: The description of motion is the same in all reference frames, regardless of their relative motion.
options.D: Two observers in different inertial frames may assign different velocities to the same object.

mcqs.answer: The description of motion is the same in all reference frames, regardless of their relative motion.
mcqs.explanation: Option C is a misconception. While the laws of physics are the same in all inertial frames, the numerical description of motion (position, velocity, etc.) changes with the frame’s relative motion. Options A, B and D are correct statements about reference frames.

mcqs.question: Particle A is at x = 2 m on a straight line and particle B is at x = 7 m on the same line (positive x direction to the right). What is the relative position of B with respect to A?

options.D: 0 m (they are at the same point)

mcqs.explanation: Relative position of B with respect to A is r_{B/A}=x_B−x_A=7 m−2 m=5 m in the positive x direction. Option A gives this value; the other options either reverse the direction or give an incorrect magnitude.

mcqs.question: Car A moves eastward with a speed of 20 m/s and Car B moves eastward with a speed of 15 m/s along the same straight road. Which statement correctly describes their relative velocities?

options.A: Velocity of A relative to B is 5 m/s east, and velocity of B relative to A is 5 m/s east.
options.B: Velocity of A relative to B is 5 m/s east, and velocity of B relative to A is 5 m/s west.
options.C: Velocity of A relative to B is 35 m/s east, and velocity of B relative to A is 35 m/s west.
options.D: Both relative velocities are zero because they move in the same direction.

mcqs.answer: Velocity of A relative to B is 5 m/s east, and velocity of B relative to A is 5 m/s west.
mcqs.explanation: Relative velocity of A with respect to B is v_A−v_B = 20 m/s − 15 m/s = 5 m/s east. Conversely, B with respect to A is v_B−v_A = –5 m/s, i.e., 5 m/s west. Option B states this correctly. Option A gives the wrong direction for B relative to A; C exaggerates the magnitude; D is false because the speeds differ.

mcqs.question: A river flows due south at 3 m/s. A boat can travel at 4 m/s relative to the water and is aimed directly east. What is the speed of the boat relative to the ground and its direction measured south of east?
mcqs.explanation: The eastward component is 4 m/s, the southward component is 3 m/s. Resultant speed = √(4²+3²)=5 m/s. The angle south of east is tan⁻¹(3/4)=36.87°,≈36.9°. Option A matches both magnitude and direction. Options B, C, D have either wrong magnitude or wrong angle.
